posts.post: King of Portugal

case_links.role: granted the brazilwood lease (head of Crown)
case_links.detail: Lease to Fernão de Loronha's Lisbon consortium, reconstructed from a letter of 3 Oct 1502; terms differ between sources (see case).

posts.post: King of Portugal

case_links.role: issued the hereditary captaincies (head of Crown)
case_links.detail: Captaincies created 1534-1536 (pt.wikipedia); the page does not name the king personally. Charters per the case file.

case_links.role: head of Crown during first Brazilian sesmaria/donatário system
case_links.detail: Donatários distributed sesmarias; the sesmaria law itself dates from 1375 (Fernando I), per the case file.

case_links.role: Crown held the dízimos as Grand Master of the Order of Christ
case_links.detail: Case file: papal grant of Julius III; not confirmed on the opened pages (the pt.wikipedia captaincies page does not cover the dizimos).

people.name: Pedro II of Portugal (Prince Regent 1668-83, king 1683-1706)

posts.post: Prince Regent, later King of Portugal

case_links.role: Crown (regent Pedro) decreed on 14 July 1674 the Junta da Administracao do Tabaco
case_links.detail: Novais thesis: 'a Coroa decretou' the Junta in 1674; it names the Crown, not the person. The estanco label is the case file's.

posts.post: King of Portugal

case_links.role: head of Crown during the gold quinto/capitação regime
case_links.detail: Capitação applied 1735 to c.1751 per the case file.

case_links.role: head of Crown during the diamond contracts
case_links.detail: Contracts held mostly by the Fernandes de Oliveira and Caldeira Brant families, per the case file.

posts.post: King of Portugal

case_links.role: chartered the Companhia Geral do Grão-Pará e Maranhão (1755)
case_links.detail: Royal charter of a joint-stock monopoly company, per the case file.

case_links.role: chartered the Companhia Geral de Pernambuco e Paraíba (1759)
case_links.detail: Charter date 13 Aug 1759 (Wikipedia) or 30 July (another source).

case_links.role: royal orders for sequestration and resale of Jesuit estates
case_links.detail: Alvará of 25 Feb 1761 put the goods in the Real Fazenda, per the case file.

case_links.role: head of Crown when Real Extração replaced the contracts (1771)
case_links.detail: Decree of 12 Aug 1771 reported by CartaCapital only.

case_links.role: head of Crown for the 1751 Mesas de Inspeção reform
case_links.detail: Per the case file.

case_links.role: head of Crown when foundry houses were re-established (order of 3 Dec 1750)
case_links.detail: Per the case file.

people.name: Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, Marquis of Pombal

posts.post: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and War
Secretary of State for Internal Affairs (de facto chief minister)

people.before: Portuguese ambassador to Great Britain 29 Nov 1738 - 25 Sep 1745 (appointed by John V); ambassador to the Holy Roman Empire (Vienna) 1745-1749.
people.after: Lost power after Joseph I's death (24 Feb 1777) under Maria I; stripped of offices and exiled to his estates; died 8 May 1782.

foreign_ties.detail: Portuguese ambassador in London 1738-1745 (Wikipedia). This is a career link, not evidence of improper dealings.

case_links.role: founded the company (Wikipedia names him as founder)
case_links.detail: Case file lists José I and Pombal as the government; he was also brother of the governor of Grão-Pará (see p-mendonca-furtado).

case_links.role: founded the company (Wikipedia names him as founder)
case_links.detail: Case file lists José I and Pombal.

case_links.role: minister in charge of the Jesuit sequestration and resale
case_links.detail: Case file lists José I and minister Pombal.

case_links.role: minister when the contract regime became Real Extração (1771) and the Regimento Diamantino was issued
case_links.detail: Per the case file.

case_links.role: minister behind the 1751 tobacco reforms; his Dedução Compendiosa is the source for contract prices
case_links.detail: Per the case file.

controversies.what: Accused after 1777 of abuse of power and tyrannical conduct, and prosecuted (Wikipedia).
controversies.outcome: Stripped of his offices, prosecuted and exiled to his estates, where he died in 1782 (Wikipedia summary).

people.name: Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado

posts.post: Governor-general of Grão-Pará and Maranhão
Secretary of State for Navy and Overseas

people.before: Brother of the Marquis of Pombal (pt.wikipedia).

case_links.role: governor of the region during the company's founding
case_links.detail: Governor 1751-1759; received instruction to create a trading company for Grao-Para (pt.wikipedia). Company chartered 1755 while he governed; his drafting role not documented.

sources.title: pt.wikipedia: Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado

posts.post: Queen of Portugal

case_links.role: ordered the Companhia Geral do Grao-Para e Maranhao shut down (1778)
case_links.detail: Wikipedia: after Pombal fell, Maria I ordered the company shut down in 1778.

posts.post: Prince Regent of Portugal (de facto from 1792, formally from 1799)
King of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves

foreign_ties.detail: British squadron arrived at Lisbon in Nov 1807 to escort the royal family to Brazil (Wikipedia); loan contracted with Great Britain on 21 April 1809 (Cardoso, scielo); 1810 treaty with Britain.

case_links.role: Prince Regent whose alvara of 12 Oct 1808 founded the Banco do Brasil (statutes signed by D. Fernando Jose de Portugal)
case_links.detail: pt.wikipedia: alvara of 12 Oct 1808 by the Prince Regent, on Linhares' suggestion. The claim that a decree of 23 Mar 1821 made its liabilities national debt was not confirmed on an opened page and is removed.

case_links.role: opened the ports (1808) and approved the 1810 treaty of commerce
case_links.detail: Open-ports policy of 1808 and the 1810 treaty (15% on British goods) confirmed on Wikipedia; the page does not name the Prince Regent personally.

case_links.role: Prince Regent when the whaling contract ended (alvará of 24 April 1801, date unconfirmed)
case_links.detail: Alvara of 24 April 1801 not confirmed on an opened page (the UFSC page was opened but states no 1801 alvara; USP page could not be opened).

case_links.role: Prince Regent when the salt estanco ended (alvará of 24 April 1801, date unconfirmed)
case_links.detail: Alvara of 24 April 1801 not confirmed on an opened page (the UFSC page was opened but states no 1801 alvara; USP page could not be opened).

people.name: Rodrigo de Sousa Coutinho, Count of Linhares

posts.post: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and War (Rio de Janeiro; pt.wikipedia lists 'Ministro da Guerra do Brasil')

people.before: Portuguese diplomat and minister; earlier Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and War (1801).
people.after: Died in Rio de Janeiro on 26 Jan 1812 while minister.

foreign_ties.detail: Portuguese side of the 1810 treaty negotiation with Britain.

case_links.role: minister credited with making the 1810 treaty with England possible
case_links.detail: pt.wikipedia says he was responsible for stimulating the creation of the Banco do Brasil and enabling the 1810 treaty.

case_links.role: credited with stimulating the creation of the Banco do Brasil
case_links.detail: Per pt.wikipedia.

people.name: Fernando José de Portugal e Castro, Count (later Marquis) of Aguiar

posts.post: Minister assisting the cabinet, president of the Real Erario, secretary of state for Brazil (title in the 1808 alvara); pt.wikipedia: Secretario de Estado dos Negocios do Reino 1808-1817

people.before: Viceroy of Brazil 1801-1806; governor of Bahia 1788-1801.
people.after: Died in Rio de Janeiro on 24 Jan 1817.

case_links.role: signed the statutes of the Banco do Brasil and acted as the bank's director
case_links.detail: Alvará of 12 Oct 1808 names the statutes 'signed by D. Fernando José de Portugal, president of the Real Erário'; Cardoso names him among the bank's directors in 1810.

sources.title: pt.wikipedia: Fernando José de Portugal e Castro

people.name: Percy Smythe, 6th Viscount Strangford

posts.post: British envoy to the Portuguese court in Rio de Janeiro
posts.appointed_by: UK government (appointed envoy to the Portuguese court in Brazil on 16 April 1808)

people.before: British envoy to Portugal 1806-1808; helped coordinate the court's transfer to Brazil.

foreign_ties.detail: Represented British interests; associated with negotiating the 1810 treaty.

case_links.role: British negotiator of the 1810 treaty
case_links.detail: Wikipedia: 'associated with the negotiation' of the treaty.

posts.post: Prince Regent of Brazil
Emperor of Brazil

foreign_ties.detail: Brazilian officials renewed the 1810 commercial treaty in 1827 (Pereira, Estudos Economicos).

case_links.role: reigning emperor when the 1827 treaty was concluded
case_links.detail: Treaty valid 15 years from ratification, per the case file.

case_links.role: as Prince Regent, sesmarias suspended in 1822 (Resolution 76)
case_links.detail: Resolution attributed to José Bonifácio per the case file; day unconfirmed.

case_links.role: reigning emperor when the first Banco do Brasil was liquidated (law of September 1829)
case_links.detail: Per the case file.

case_links.role: reigning emperor at the company's founding (1830); no state grant or decision identified
case_links.detail: Case file: private sale and joint-stock company.

people.name: José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva

posts.post: Minister of the Kingdom and Foreign Affairs

case_links.role: attributed author of Resolution 76 (1822) suspending sesmarias
case_links.detail: Attribution from the case file; the day (17 July 1822) was not seen on an opened page.

posts.post: British Foreign Secretary
posts.appointed_by: King George IV (cabinet of Lord Liverpool)

foreign_ties.detail: British Foreign Secretary during the Brazil treaty talks.

case_links.role: British Foreign Secretary; argued in 1826 that the commercial treaty was advantageous to Britain and 'more onerous to Brazil'
case_links.detail: Quote per Pereira (Estudos Economicos); the article says 'the commercial treaty' (the 1810 regime that was renewed in 1827). Canning died 8 Aug 1827.

posts.post: Emperor of Brazil
posts.appointed_by: hereditary; regency until declared of age in 1840

foreign_ties.counterpart: British companies (São Paulo Railway Company, Rio de Janeiro Gas Company; both London-incorporated)
foreign_ties.detail: Decreto 2.601 (1860) and Decreto 3.456 (1865) carry the Emperor's rubrica. This is a record of concessions, not of personal gain. The telegraph and steam-navigation concessions listed earlier were not confirmed on opened pages and are removed.

case_links.role: reigning emperor; Lei 601 sanctioned 1850
case_links.detail: Carta de Lei with rubrica; see Monte Alegre. Decree/law bears 'Com Rubrica de Sua Magestade o Imperador' (opened).

case_links.role: reigning emperor; Decreto 3.456 (1865) authorised the London-based Rio de Janeiro Gas Company Limited
case_links.detail: Decree signed by the minister of Agriculture. Decree/law bears 'Com Rubrica de Sua Magestade o Imperador' (opened).

case_links.role: reigning emperor; Decreto 1.037 (1852) gave the steam navigation privilege to Mauá
case_links.detail: Per the decree. Decree/law bears 'Com Rubrica de Sua Magestade o Imperador' (opened).

case_links.role: reigning emperor; Decreto 641 (1852), Decreto 2.601 (1860) approving the London articles of the São Paulo Railway
case_links.detail: Per the decrees. Decree/law bears 'Com Rubrica de Sua Magestade o Imperador' (opened).

case_links.role: reigning emperor; 1873 submarine telegraph concessions
case_links.detail: Telegraph concessions of 1873: the cited page returned 403 and could not be opened.

people.name: José da Costa Carvalho, Viscount (later Marquis) of Monte Alegre

posts.post: President of the Council of Ministers (cabinet of 8 Oct 1849; also Minister of the Empire 1848-1852)

case_links.role: head of government; Lei 601 carta de lei is signed 'Visconde de Mont'alegre'
case_links.detail: Per the original publication.

people.name: Eusébio de Queirós Coutinho Matoso Câmara

posts.post: Minister of Justice (and so Chancellor in the Lei 601 sealing chain)

case_links.role: signed the Lei 601 carta de lei chain as Eusebio de Queiroz (Minister of Justice)
case_links.detail: His name appears in the chain; his role in drafting the law is not documented. (He is known for the 1850 anti-slave-trade law, a different act.)

case_links.role: signed Decreto 641 (interest guarantee)
case_links.detail: Decreto 641 (26 June 1852) is signed by him; it also orders a refund to Thomaz Cochrane, whose nationality is unconfirmed (removed as a foreign tie).

case_links.role: signed Decreto 1.037 (Amazon steam navigation contract)
case_links.detail: Per the decree.

case_links.detail: Per the decree.
